context: a letter from W. E. Darwin, which you are answering
exchanges:
I counted a pod this morning as carefully as possible by tens sweeping away the tens each time. it is rather a job. in a little bit of paper enclosed I send a sample of the seeds I counted, though with some misgivings whether I ought not to omit them

tell me whether you consider them sterile or not. Any worse than those I did not count. I am afraid you’ll have a job to open the paper

Your affect son | WE Darwin

There were only 5 seeds in packet sent; these were all perfectly good—

But do not bother yourself & count anymore; from long practice I can do it very quickly: I have counted about 30 pods of wild—20 of home-grown; besides my artificially fertilised pods. So I have had lots of counting! Next year I shall make 136 more crosses, so I shall have counting with a vengeance next year.—

Good Bye | My dear old man | C. D
